`FINDING_ID:` IM_F101  
`SEVERITY:` 0.96  
`FLAW_CLASS:` 5  
`ABSTRACTION_INDEX:` 0.88  
`DESCRIPTION:` Level-3 self-diagnosis is unreachable under the default protocol.  
`PROPOSED_FIX:` Remove the blanket `current_round < 5` gate and let each self-check enforce its own evidence threshold.  
`VERIFIED:` TRUE  

`FIND:` At [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4034](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4034), `self_diagnose()` returns immediately while `current_round < 5`. The default protocol is `max_rounds = 5` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L116](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L116), and `process_round()` uses zero-based round indices from `_process_round_count` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5353](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5353). In a default run, the last round index is `4`, so the whole Exp15b self-adjustment layer is dead code.

`FIX:`

Once that dead gate is removed, the next defect becomes live immediately: those checks still trigger on event counts rather than sustained bad rounds, which is IM_F102 below.

`FINDING_ID:` IM_F103

`DESCRIPTION:` Model-scoped remediations are applied and verified against the global system `finding_count`, often using the previous round’s total, not the affected model’s current output.  
`PROPOSED_FIX:` Thread `model_id` through remediation state and resolve `finding_count` from that model’s own history when the diagnosis is model-scoped.  
`VERIFIED:` TRUE  

`FIND:` Several model-specific chains target `finding_count`, for example `model_failure` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5957](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5957), `parser_yield` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5989](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5989), `monotonic_decline` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L6001](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6001), and `cpf_spike` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L6013](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6013). Those model diagnoses are applied before `record_round()` runs at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5509](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5509), so the “current” global finding count is usually the previous round’s total. `FIND:` Model-specific diagnoses reuse shared `pathology_key` values: `model_failure` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L3070](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3070), `dispatch_false_positive` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4348](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4348), and `verification_miscalibration` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4404](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4404). But `apply_diagnosis()` reads and writes `_remediation_state` only by `chain_key` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L6229](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6229) and [bench/dynamic_management.py#L6338](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6338), `set_remediation_state()` stores only that key at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L3224](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3224), and `record_remediation_outcome()` pools effectiveness by the same key at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L3383](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3383). 5.
`FINDING_ID:` IM_F105  
`SEVERITY:` 0.87  
`FLAW_CLASS:` 5  
`ABSTRACTION_INDEX:` 0.72  
`DESCRIPTION:` `process_round()` feeds `record_model_round()` a failure flag that misses actual TIMEOUT, EMPTY, and FORMAT failures.  
`PROPOSED_FIX:` Derive `failed` from the already-computed `failure_type`, not from a parseability shortcut.  
`VERIFIED:` TRUE  

`FIND:` `process_round()` computes authoritative failure types first at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5371](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5371). But when it later calls `record_model_round()`, it throws that away and uses `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable` at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L5481](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5481). `record_model_round()` uses `failed` to drive consecutive failure tracking at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L3041](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3041). So a parseable slow response can be `FailureType.TIMEOUT` in Area 6, yet `failed=False` in the immune monitor; repeated TIMEOUT/EMPTY/FORMAT failures never accumulate into `model_failure`.

`FIX:`
```text
<<<<
            fc = _model_finding_counts.get(mid, 0)
            failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable
            resp = responses.get(mid)
====
            fc = _model_finding_counts.get(mid, 0)
            resp = responses.get(mid)
            failure_type = failures.get(mid)
            failed = failure_type in {
                FailureType.EMPTY,
                FailureType.TIMEOUT,
                FailureType.MALFORMED,
                FailureType.FORMAT,
            }
>>>>
```

`FOLLOW:` This makes the Level-2 `model_failure` pathology at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L3050](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3050) respond to actual transport/protocol failures instead of only “missing or unparseable” responses. Missing-response handling still needs proper dispatched-model scoping; that is a separate adjacency issue and not solved by this fix.

6.
`FINDING_ID:` IM_F106  
`SEVERITY:` 0.76  
`FLAW_CLASS:` 2  
`ABSTRACTION_INDEX:` 0.54  
`DESCRIPTION:` `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` never emits the `UNDERPERFORM` event, despite the event type existing and all other failure classes emitting events.  
`PROPOSED_FIX:` Emit `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` before returning `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM`.  
`VERIFIED:` TRUE  

`FIND:` `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` exists at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4999](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4999). `detect_failure()` emits events for EMPTY, TIMEOUT, MALFORMED, and FORMAT at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4544](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4544), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4550](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4550), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4556](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4556), and [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4566](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4566). But the UNDERPERFORM branch at [bench/dynamic_management.py#L4587](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4587) returns `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM` directly with no event emission. That creates an observability hole for the one failure class driven by rolling history.

`FIX:`
```text
<<<<
            if underperform_count / len(recent_perfs) >= self.config.eta_underperform:
                return FailureType.UNDERPERFORM
====
            if underperform_count / len(recent_perfs) >= self.config.eta_underperform:
                self._emit_event(
                    ManagerEvent(
                        event_type=ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM,
                        model_id=response.model_id,
                        round_idx=response.round_idx,
                        detail=(
                            f"Performance ratio {perf:.3f} below threshold "
                            f"{self.config.theta_under:.3f} in "
                            f"{underperform_count}/{len(recent_perfs)} recent rounds"
                        ),
                    )
                )
                return FailureType.UNDERPERFORM
>>>>
```

`FOLLOW:` Event-stream consumers will now see UNDERPERFORM transitions the same way they already see EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT. No recovery policy changes are required, but PM monitoring, logs, and any downstream alerting keyed on `ManagerEventType` become consistent.

I stopped at these six because the next candidates either overlap the prior list you provided or need non-boundary code to choose a non-speculative fix. The strongest two are IM_F103 and IM_F104; they break the identity and measurement contracts for model-specific remediations.
